subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & operational impacts
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & operational impacts

Hi Andrew — thanks again for a great demo earlier today. Quick recap and the recommended next steps from our side so your team can review and share with engineering/ops.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Outcome: three candidate model tiers that balance your latency target (<=120ms p50 for single-turn API calls) and extraction quality for invoice/billing items.
- Action: please review the shortlist below and confirm which 1) you want us to pilot and 2) whether you prefer Hosted vs Dedicated for the pilot.

Recommended shortlist (rationale + expected operational impact)
1) Mistral-7B-8k (quantized 4-bit) — "Quality-first / moderate cost"
   - Why: best tradeoff for structured extraction in our prompt runs (F1 ~0.86 on our prompt set), robust on edge-case date formats.
   - Latency: ~80–110ms p50 on our Dedicated 1xA100 profile; p95 ~220ms.
   - Cost profile: ~0.012 USD per 1k tokens (in Dedicated); lower in hosted burst.
   - Risk: slightly higher token consumption for long context; regression risk low based on our evals.

2) Llama-2-13B-QLoRA (8k) — "High-quality, higher cost"
   - Why: top quality on hallucination-sensitive tasks, F1 ~0.89 on extraction set; better recall.
   - Latency: ~140–180ms p50 on similar infra; p95 ~380ms (may exceed your 120ms target without aggressive batching / Dedicated single-tenant sizing).
   - Cost: ~0.028 USD per 1k tokens.
   - Risk: higher 95th percentile latency; recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity if chosen.

3) Redwood-R1-3.3B-INT8 (low-latency fallback) — "Cost-first / low-latency"
   - Why: strong p50 latency, stable throughput for spikes; F1 ~0.80 (lower recall on complex nested line items).
   - Latency: ~35–60ms p50; p95 ~110ms.
   - Cost: ~0.006 USD per 1k tokens.
   - Risk: may require a two-stage pipeline (fast run + verify with larger model) for sensitive billing rules.

Benchmarks and artifacts attached / linked
- Attached: prompt_pack_v1.zip (representative prompt templates + sample extraction examples)
- Attached: benchmarks_summary_may17.csv (summary metrics across candidate models)
- Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-prompt-pack
- Internal benchmark dashboard: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/DEAL-3842

Quality/regression concerns (short)
- Hallucination/false positives: Llama-2-13B shows best recall but still requires strict prompt templates and negative examples in the eval suite.
- Tokenization drift: the larger models consume more tokens for the same prompt; we included normalized prompt variants in prompt_pack_v1.zip.
- Monitoring: recommend running the first 48 hours of pilot with Golden Set checks (we can wire this into Redwood Console for per-request quality alerts).

Pilot recommendation and next steps
1) Pilot target: choose 1 model (we recommend Mistral-7B if you prioritize balanced cost/quality).
2) Mode: start Hosted for fastest setup, or Dedicated if you need p95 guarantees and isolated capacity.
3) Pilot scope: 2-week evaluation, 50k API calls/day simulated (we can loadgen).
4) Deliverables: evaluation report, live Dashboard access, suggested prompt guardrails, and a regression-alert set.

Questions for your team
- Do you need on-prem / VPC for the pilot? If yes, there will be a slightly longer setup (~2–3 weeks).
- Are you comfortable starting with Hosted and moving to Dedicated if p95 latency or throughput becomes a blocker?

Next actions
- If you confirm model + mode, we’ll provision a pilot and share test credentials + sandbox dataset.
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Karthik) to go over batching, KV cache behavior, and observability hooks.

Thanks — attaching the prompt pack and benchmark CSV for review. Happy to jump on a quick follow-up later today if that helps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Thanks Kim — very helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) On hallucination / false positive counts: can you share the concrete precision/recall numbers for the billing-extraction Golden Set (we saw F1 but want the breakdown)?

2) For latency: our product SLA target is 95th <= 300ms (burst tolerant), but for interactive UI flows we want p50 <= 120ms. You mentioned Llama-2-13B p95 ~380ms — is that on Hosted or Dedicated? Would tuning batching or KV cache lower that p95 materially?

3) For the pilot, we definitely want to avoid a long setup. Hosted is preferred unless the p95 on the chosen model is a hard blocker. If we pick Llama-2-13B, can you estimate the Dedicated sizing needed to hit p95 <= 300ms?

4) Can you include one sample prompt template tailored to our billing-extraction use case (we’ll try it against 500 records)?

Also looping in our engineering manager Sam (sam@sidereal.ai) for any infra-related questions.

Thanks — we’re aiming to lock the pilot model by EOD Wednesday (5/19).

—Andrew

Thanks Andrew — answers inline below and I attached a quick example prompt (extraction_template.json) inside prompt_pack_v1.zip.

1) Precision / Recall (billing-extraction Golden Set, 1,200 labeled lines):
   - Mistral-7B-8k: Precision 0.84, Recall 0.88 (F1 0.86)
   - Llama-2-13B-QLoRA: Precision 0.87, Recall 0.92 (F1 0.89)
   - Redwood-R1-3.3B-INT8: Precision 0.78, Recall 0.83 (F1 0.80)
   - Notes: we converted all date/amount formats to canonical forms in evaluation to avoid tokenization skew. Full per-case breakdown is in benchmarks_summary_may17.csv.

2) Latency context: the numbers I quoted were on Dedicated single-tenant instances with the baseline infra profile (1xA100 equivalent). Hosted numbers vary slightly due to multi-tenant packing — Llama-2-13B p95 ~380ms was observed on Hosted; on Dedicated with reserved capacity we’ve measured p95 as low as ~280–300ms depending on input length.
   - Batching/KV cache: KV cache helps multi-turn flows more than single-turn extraction. Batching does reduce unit cost but can increase p95 latency if you wait to accumulate tokens. For your interactive UI, keep batching minimal and prioritize Dedicated to shrink variability.

3) Dedicated sizing estimate (target: Llama-2-13B p95 <= 300ms):
   - Recommendation: Dedicated c2 profile (2xA100 sized pool) for steady 50–60 qps with p95 ~280–300ms. If you expect spikes, add a small burst pool (50% capacity) or enable autoscale with warm nodes.

4) Sample prompt template: included in prompt_pack_v1.zip as extraction_template.json. Short example below: 

"""
System: You are a precise invoice extraction assistant. Output strictly JSON matching the schema: {
  "invoice_number": string,
  "invoice_date": YYYY-MM-DD,
  "total_amount": {"value": number, "currency": string},
  "line_items": [ {"description": string, "quantity": number, "unit_price": number} ]
}

User: Parse the following raw invoice text and output the JSON above. Preserve numeric values as numbers. If a field is missing, output null.

Text: "<INVOICE_TEXT>"
"""

Pilot timeline suggestion
- If you confirm model by EOD 2027-05-19 we can spin up Hosted sandbox credentials within 24 hours. Dedicated baseline provisioning ~5 business days.

Proposed meeting: 30-min deep-dive with Karthik Wednesday 5/19 10:00–10:30am PT (we're flexible). Would that work for Sam + your infra lead?

If you confirm Mistral-7B + Hosted, we’ll provision and share test keys immediately. If you prefer Llama-2-13B, let us know and we’ll include Dedicated sizing and pricing in the follow-up quote.

Thanks — Kim
